But {{ls}}he {{ls}}aid, The head of Iohn the Bapti{{ls}}t. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=25}}† And vvhen {{ls}}he vvas gone in by and by vvith ha{{ls}}t to the King, {{ls}}he a{{ls}}keth {{ls}}aying, I vvil that forthvvith thou giue me in a platter the head of Iohn the Bapti{{ls}}t. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=26}}† And the King vvas {{ls}}troken {{ls}}ad. Becau{{ls}}e of his othe and for them that {{ls}}ate together at table he vvould not di{{ls}}plea{{ls}}e her: {{verse|chapter=6|verse=27}}† but {{ls}}ending the hangman, commaunded that his head {{ls}}hould be brought in a platter. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=28}}† And he beheaded him in the pri{{ls}}on, and brought his head in a platter: and gaue it to the dam{{ls}}el, and the dam{{ls}}el gaue it to her mother. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=29}}† Which his di{{ls}}ciples hearing came, and tooke his body: and they put it in a monument.⊣

{{verse|chapter=6|verse=30}}† And {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Lu. 9, 10.''}}* the Apo{{ls}}tles gathering together vnto Ie{{ls}}us, made relation to him of al things that they had done and taught. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=31}}† And he {{ls}}aid to them, Come apart into the de{{ls}}ert place, and re{{ls}}t a litle. For there vvere that came and vvent, many: and they had not {{ls}}o much as {{ls}}pace to eate. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=32}}† And {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 14, 13.''}}* going vp into the boate, they vvent into a de{{ls}}ert place apart. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=33}}† And they {{ls}}avv them going avvay, and many knevv: and they ranne flocking thither on foote from al cities, and preuented them.

{{verse|chapter=6|verse=34}}† And going forth, {{sc|Iesvs}} {{ls}}avv a great multitude: and he had compa{{ls}}sion on them, becau{{ls}}e they vvere as {{ls}}heepe not hauing a {{ls}}hepheard, and he began to teach them many things. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=35}}† And {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 14, 15. Lu. 9, 12. Io. 6, 5.''}}* vvhen the day vvas novv farre {{ls}}pent, his Di{{ls}}ciples came to him, {{ls}}aying, This is a de{{ls}}ert place, and the houre is novv pa{{ls}}t: {{verse|chapter=6|verse=36}}† dimi{{ls}}se them, that going out into the next villages and tovvnes, they may bie them {{ls}}elues meates to eate. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=37}}† And he an{{ls}}vvering {{ls}}aid, Giue ye them to eate. And they {{ls}}aid to him, Let vs goe and bie bread for tvvo hundred pence: and vve vvil giue them to eate. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=38}}† And he {{ls}}aith to them, Hovv many loaues haue you? goe and {{ls}}ee. And vvhen they knevv, they {{ls}}ay, Fiue, and tvvo fi{{ls}}hes. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=39}}† And he commaunded them that they {{ls}}hould make al {{ls}}it dovvne, by companies vpon the greene gra{{ls}}{{ls}}e. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=40}}† And they {{ls}}ate dovvne in rankes by hundreds and fifties. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=41}}† And vvhen he had taken the fiue loaues, and the tvvo fi{{ls}}hes: looking vp vnto heauen,<noinclude>{{rh|||he}}</noinclude>
